va_aid_box.blurb: A compact rock amphitheater in the Potomac gorge at Great Falls, just downstream of Juliet's Balcony, and one of the busiest corners of the park's cliffs. The 22 lines are mostly top-ropes, with a handful of trad leads and a single aid line. Difficulty covers the whole range: a few easy climbs in the 5.5 to 5.7 band, a solid core of 5.9 to 5.10, and a good number of 5.11 and 5.12 problems, plus a couple around 5.13. Walls here are short, roughly the height of the surrounding cliffs, and anchors are generally trees, so bring slings. Fun for confident intermediates and strong climbers alike; expect company on fair-weather weekends.

va_cow_s_hoof.blurb: A set-back group of small cliffs and boulders within Great Falls Park, reached on foot through the woods rather than along the river. The setting is cool and shady, which makes it a pleasant choice when the riverside walls bake. Of the 20 climbs here, about half are trad lines, nearly as many are boulder problems, and there is one aid route, among only a couple in the whole Great Falls area. Trad grades run from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, with most in the 5.8 to 5.10 range; boulder problems skew easy to moderate with a few hard ones. A quieter alternative to the busier crags nearby.

va_desert_pony_buttress.blurb: A sport wall tucked low in the gully below Pinnacle Rock, in the cliffs of Breaks Interstate Park in far southwest Virginia. It sits between the Pinnacle Overlook section and Ginger Wall, and its orange and tan face stands out from the surrounding stone. Twenty routes, nearly all of them bolted, with two trad lines. Grades start around 5.7 and build steadily, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits climbers who have outgrown the moderates. One arete line on the left side of the buttress is a notable long pitch with two possible lower-off points. Expect a short downhill walk in and a steep climb back out.
va_desert_pony_buttress.approach: Go down the main gully used for reaching Pinnacle Rock, then turn left at the bottom and follow the base of the cliff about 300 yards. The buttress with the prominent arete is the one you want.

va_alpha_wall.blurb: A wall in the Mile Two section of Guest River Gorge in Southwest Virginia, found up a short hill just before the Machine Gun Boulder. It holds 20 routes, about 12 sport and 8 trad, plus an easy third-class arete. The climbing is aimed at the middle of the grade scale: a cluster around 5.9 and 5.10, a healthy group of 5.11s, and a few 5.12 and 5.13 lines near the top end. The standout for most visitors is the four-star 5.10c sport route. A decent stop for a mixed party where some want to lead bolts and others want to place gear.

va_second_mountain.blurb: A small bouldering area on a wooded knob above Route 33, west of Harrisonburg in the Shenandoah Valley. The stone is quality sandstone, and the problems are scattered in a few clusters, including the Satellite Boulder with its well-known roof. Roughly twenty problems are recorded, running from V0 all the way to V10; the bulk sit in the V4 range, with a good dose of harder slabs and powerful lines above that. It is a locals' area rather than a destination, best for a day trip with a pad and some stamina, since the uphill hike is steep and the trail can be overgrown. Late summer and fall are the preferred seasons.

va_roadside.blurb: The closest bouldering to the McAfee's Knob trailhead near Catawba and Roanoke, with blocks sitting right beside the start of the fire road. The rock is sandstone, and the main boulder is a steep fin that serves as a proving ground for Southwest Virginia boulderers. Around twenty problems are recorded, from V0 through V10, with the biggest group in the middle grades and a few hard lines at the top. Good for a quick session without hiking to the knob itself, and easy to combine with a walk on the trail. Cooler months, especially late fall, are more comfortable than the hot, buggy summer.

va_rock_house_boulder.blurb: A boulder in the picnic area of Grayson Highlands State Park, in the far southwest of Virginia, directly across the lot from the larger Olympus Boulder and right beside the Rock House Loop Trail. The approach is only seconds long. Lines are slightly to heavily overhung, with a fun dihedral problem among them. About twenty problems are recorded from V0 to V7, with the largest group at the hard end and a spread of easier and mid-grade options below. A handy stop for a short session, and the park facilities nearby make it easy to bring along friends who do not climb.
